questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Going to a country with a different culture to explore, in order to expand both my academic and personal view on studying.

questions.answer: There is a bit more expenses, however it is a great opportunity to experience the real life as opposed to only being exposed to the campus and academic life.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process for courses at NTU is done through an online course selector. It was pretty easy and fairly intuitive once you learn what is up and down. However, help for the course selector is also possible through the guidance counsellors.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guidance counsellors and fellow classmates.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, only one of my courses did not begin as the number of students registered for the course was too low.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it in good time, and ask fellow students to help you if you're unsure.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses varied a lot, depending on what you are interested in. As a BA it is also possible to do some MA courses if it is something you are interested in.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were very similar with a few reports having to be handed in during the semester, and with class presentations. Other courses had weekly quizzes and attendance counting for the final grade, alongside with reports and presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Chinese Enhancing Course & General Chinese Language Course:
I would definitely recommend taking at least one Chinese Language course, as it is always fun to learn the language of the country you are living in. Furthermore, it can help in your day-to-day life. The courses offered at NTU is very well done, and you are able to learn a surprisingly lot of Mandarin in just one semester. 

International Companions for Learning:
A program that is not really a course, but more of a cultural exchange with local students from elementary schools around Taiwan. It is a weekly online meeting with a class of young students, and you also have a local student from the university as your partner. During this program you also get to go on a schooltrip to the school of your students, a trip that is fully paid by NTU. It is a great way to explore the country and dive in to the local and rural culture of Taiwan.

Exploring Taiwan: natural environment and resources & Exploring Taiwan: Natural Resources Conservation and Management:
Any course with the title "Exploring Taiwan" is a course mostly dedicated to exchange students. It is a great way to learn about the country on many different aspects.

Seminar on China and Global Climate Governance:
A course dedicated to investigate the behaviour of China in regards to how climate politics are conducted and governed. Super interesting and relevant. The professor is amazing and he is very helpful and knowledgeable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
A lot of things are fairly cheap in Taiwan compared to Denmark. Many times it is better and cheaper to go out and buy food from a nightmarket, rather than cooking at home. The public transportation runs very well, i did have to spend quite a lot of money on it monthly because i lived quite far away from my university.
But in general there was not really any unexpected costs, except for government documents if that is needed. But that depends a lot on how long you are staying and what you need to do while you're in Taiwan.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
More expensive:
Public transportation (Still very cheap, just thought it was even cheaper).

Less expensive:
Pretty much everything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Any kind of club, sport and hobbies was available to the students through the university. Very well done!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel around the island as much as possible. It is not very big, but there is still so much to see, and the landscape and topography is so diverse.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to Alishan, Yangmingshan, go to some of the smaller islands, visit Kaohsiung & Kenting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture was very different, however studying with other exchange students made it very easy to adjust, while also getting to know local students helped a lot. Taiwanese people are VERY friendly and hospitable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Give them time as some students are not too comfortable with their english, even though it is at a good level. Try to learn some Mandarin to talk with them. Join the International Companions for Learning programme.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The paperwork and bureaucracy in Taiwan is horrible.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people, the food, the architecture and landscapes and the academic life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn a bit of Mandarin.
Be open-minded to a different culture.
Focus on the life outside of school the most.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in another country and enjoying a life that is so different from the one that is known back in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Prolonging the stay for a second semester. If you have thoughts about this make sure that you inform KU and NTU a long time in advance so they can make sure everything is in order.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your trip!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
